This character appears defeated and overshadowed by a looming figure. The scene conveys a sense of movement and intent, with dynamic gestures from the surrounding figures. The composition contrasts dark shading on the left with lighter figures on the right. The title "Le triomphe du Paganisme" hints at the triumph of paganism over religious themes.

artworks.title: Manquant le convoi
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows three exaggerated figures in a rainstorm rushing towards a departing train. The figures are comically drawn with large heads and expressive faces, battling the rain with diagonal lines. One figure wears a top hat, another holds an umbrella in the wrong direction, and the third figure is small and huddled. They are all trying to catch a train in the background, depicted simplistically. The landscape includes a train station or buildings. The caption implies they missed their connection, adding to the humor of the scene. The style is cartoonish and satirical, likely humorously depicting travel challenges in the railway age.

The individuals are depicted in vintage attire, such as top hats and bonnets, reminiscent of the 19th century. The crowd appears to be rushing towards train carriages. The composition conveys a sense of urgency and motion, with figures in mid-action. The style resembles that of Honoré Daumier.

The expressions on their faces suggest a critical or scrutinizing gaze as they view the art pieces. The composition is dense, filled with the overlapping forms of the observers.

The image is divided into two sections: the upper section shows three figures sipping from a shared large glass using straws, while the lower section shows two figures drinking directly from glasses. The upper section shows the figures leaning over a small round table to sip together, while the lower section shows a more laid-back approach, with one figure resting their head on their hand. The drawing uses a monochromatic palette with detailed line work typical of satirical illustrations.

The leftmost figure wears a pointed helmet with writing on the front, the middle figure has a tight blindfold, and the rightmost figure wears a wrap around its head. They lean slightly towards each other. The title of the drawing is "Trois Pauvres aveugles" meaning "Three Poor Blind Men." The style is reminiscent of 19th-century satirical works.
